reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate. (1) No null arm: 'structured vs random' has no random-vs-random control. Measured on a 3-uniform coverage model at B=1024 (400 trials): threshold mean 2554 relations, sd 414 (16.2%). With 20 bases per arm the SE of a difference of means is ~5.1%, larger than the 3% 'within' band, so a true null fails the prediction_if_false test about half the time, and a 10% effect is only ~2 sigma. (2) Relation supply: at p~2^20, B=1024, m=2 the expected number of zero-sum triples of base points is B^3/(6p) ~ 171, far below the ~2550 relations needed for full rank (threshold is coupon-collector/min-degree dominated, ~ (B/3)(ln B + gamma), not the 0.918 B XORSAT core threshold). Full rank is unreachable with base-only triples; targets R=aP+bQ must be added as extra vertices, and then 'full rank' (on base columns) and the hypergraph uniformity must be defined. (3) 'Structured t-design basis' and 'F' are undefined, so the >=10% prediction has no concrete treatment arm; arithmetic-progression/subgroup-like bases have known logs and trivial rank deficiency, a confound. (4) Metric (relations to rank B-1 mod a prime l | r) is structural/counted, good; runtime fine (pair-sum table 524k vectorised adds per base, seconds), but r must be chosen with a large prime factor. (5) Scaling: the toy tests only the constant in front of B ln B; the mean-yield wall is untouched and per-relation oracle cost D, not relation count, governs the B*D^2 vs N certificate, so even a positive result is accounting/constant factor and says nothing about n=131 beyond a ln-B-dependent constant unless B is scanned.
fix: Redesign: (a) Model the threshold on the hypergraph directly: simulate/measure relations-to-full-rank mod prime l (l | r, l>2^16) for degree sequences, using common random numbers (same edge stream order, paired differences). (b) Arms: A0 uniform random base (null1) vs independent uniform random base (null2) to calibrate noise; T = degree-shaped base defined operationally (e.g. choose base points so that the vertex-degree distribution in the relation graph has variance ratio v in {0.5,1,2} times Poisson, via greedy selection from a larger candidate pool using actual sum-table degrees); optional structured arm = t-design/coset base, with rank taken after excluding known-log structure. (c) Real-curve part: prime-order curve with p~2^20 (PARI ellcard), B in {256,512,1024,2048,4096}; build pair-sum dict per base (numpy, vectorised Fermat inverse, int64 safe since p<2^21); relations = decompositions of random targets R=aP+bQ, edge=(R,P1,P2), vertices = base + targets; success metric = number of relations until rank over GF(l) of the base-column restriction after eliminating target columns reaches B-1 (also report min-degree-zero count, rank deficiency at fixed 2.0*B*ln B relations). (d) Statistics: >=200 bases per arm for the pure hypergraph sim (seconds) and >=40 on real curves; declare effect iff paired difference CI excludes 0 and |effect| >= 10% beyond the null1-vs-null2 spread; prediction_if_false: CI within +-3%. (e) Scale: fit relations_needed = c*B*(ln B + g) across B and report c per arm; claim only the shift in c (a constant) and state that it cannot move exponent or B*D^2 vs N. Budget: sim <2 CPU-min, real-curve <15 CPU-min with python3+numpy+cypari2; no msolve/SAT needed. Classification stays accounting.
